* Fixes to watcher consumer logging and to the cached ``pod_manager``
context under Kubernetes. See #2805, #2806, and #2809.
* The documentation now marks both modes as stable. See #2865.

Breaking Changes

* The unused ``DBT_NO_TESTS_MSG`` and ``DBT_WARN_MSG`` constants and the
module-level logger have been removed from ``cosmos.dbt.parser.output``
as part of a parser cleanup. If your custom code imported them, inline
the literals (``"Nothing to do"`` / ``"WARN"``) instead. See #2832.

Behaviour Changes

These changes adjust observable behaviour. None of them break the
documented public API, but review them before upgrading — especially if
you rely on ephemeral models running dbt.

* Ephemeral dbt models now render as ``EmptyOperator`` by default
(``RenderConfig.ephemeral_models_as_empty_operator=True``). They no
longer run dbt or emit datasets/assets, callbacks, OpenLineage events,
or compiled SQL. Set
``RenderConfig(ephemeral_models_as_empty_operator=False)`` to restore
the previous behaviour. See #2759.
* ``on_warning_callback`` now fires for dbt test warnings in
``ExecutionMode.LOCAL`` subprocess mode (previously skipped on dbt
1.10+, where ``PASS=.. WARN=N`` is no longer the final stdout line). See
#2832.
* The output-only template fields ``compiled_sql`` and ``freshness`` are
now rejected with ``CosmosValueError`` at task instantiation if passed
via ``operator_args`` or directly to a local operator (they were
previously overwritten by Cosmos at runtime, so any value silently had
no effect); the guard covers both the synchronous local operators and
the async BigQuery path. See #2726 and #2852.
* ``RenderConfig.exclude`` is now applied to per-model and detached test
tasks under ``TestBehavior.AFTER_EACH`` and ``BUILD`` (previously only
the ``AFTER_ALL`` aggregate test task honoured it), so exclusions such
as ``exclude=["resource_type:unit_test"]`` now take effect without an
``operator_args`` workaround. See #2850.

## Summary

Cuts **1.15.0 GA** from the `release-1.15.0` head branch. Base branch is
`main`.

One head branch and one PR span the whole effort (`a1 → a2 → a3 →
1.15.0`). Each alpha synced `main` to pull the cycle's work forward;
**after `a3` the branch was frozen** by team agreement, so no further
`main` merges land here — only targeted cherry-picks if final testing
surfaces a fix. GA therefore ships exactly the **162 PRs** validated
through `a3`.

**Headline for this release:** `ExecutionMode.WATCHER` and
`ExecutionMode.WATCHER_KUBERNETES` are promoted from experimental to
**stable**, effective Cosmos 1.15.0 (#2865).

## Milestone

[Cosmos
1.15.0](https://github.com/astronomer/astronomer-cosmos/milestone/45) —
**162 merged PRs, 0 open items**. Everything in the milestone is merged;
the remaining in-flight work from earlier cuts (#2767, #2486, #1625,
#1563) was **deferred to `Cosmos 1.16.0`**, and #2006 was closed.

changelog convention, the `Now Stable` / `Breaking Changes` / `Behaviour

## What

Airflow 3.3.0 is now GA. Follows up on #2831, which added Airflow 3.3
(then beta) to the test
matrix with a temporary live-resolution branch in
`scripts/test/pre-install-airflow.sh` (moving
`constraints-3-3` branch + `apache-airflow>=3.3.0b1,<3.4.0
--prerelease=allow`), so 3.3 could be

- Add `requirements/requirements-airflow-3.3-dbt-1.11.txt`, sourced from
a real `ubuntu-latest` CI
`pip freeze` (the "Install packages and dependencies" step of a post-GA
`Run-Integration-Tests`
job, python 3.10), with the host-specific editable Cosmos install line
stripped. Installing this
file standalone forces a full dependency resolution rather than the
incremental,
never-cross-validated installs the live branch used, which surfaced

AWS SDK family

plus

`scripts/test/pre-install-airflow.sh` down to the
single `uv pip install -r requirements/...` line used by 3.0-3.2,
dropping the constraint-URL
download, `--prerelease=allow`, the extra `apache-airflow-devel-common`
install, and the
temporary `gcsfs<2026` curation (no longer needed since the pinned file
bakes in a compatible
  `gcsfs`).
- A follow-up commit fixes conflicts specific to Python >=3.11 that a
single-python (3.10) freeze
can't surface: `google-cloud-aiplatform` tightens its
`google-cloud-storage` floor to `>=3.10.0`
only under a `python_version>="3.13"` marker (incompatible with our
`google-cloud-storage==3.1.1`,
capped low by `dbt-bigquery`) — downgraded to `1.148.1`, the last
version with the looser
`python_version>="3.13"` floor, with `litellm`/`google-genai` adjusted
to match its narrower
extras. Also dropped `backports-datetime-fromisoformat` and
`backports.strenum`, both real
`pip freeze` entries gated by `python_version < "3.11"` markers that a
flat requirements file
can't preserve — they fail to build on Python 3.13 if force-installed
there, and aren't present
  in the analogous 3.2 file either.

subject: Add dbt-core 1.12 to test matrix (#2773)
message:
Add dbt-core 1.12 to test matrix (#2773)

## Summary

Adds **dbt-core 1.12 (stable, `1.12.0`)** to the Cosmos test matrix
**and wires the CI install path** so the new version is actually
exercised in CI rather than left as a no-op matrix label.

Supersedes the closed preparatory PR #2754 (which only added the Hatch
matrix slot while `1.12` was pre-release / blocked on `dbt-loom`).

## Why this is more than a one-line matrix bump

The unit and integration jobs install dbt from **pinned
`requirements/requirements-airflow-X.Y-dbt-Z.txt` lockfiles**, not from
the matrix value directly. Before this PR every Airflow version
installed the hardcoded `…-dbt-1.11.txt` file regardless of the matrix
`dbt-version`, so adding `"1.12"` to the matrix alone would install dbt
1.11 under a "1.12" label. To make CI genuinely run 1.12 the install
path now selects the lockfile by `(airflow, dbt)`.

## Touchpoints applied

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` | `[tool.hatch.envs.tests.matrix].dbt` — inserted
`"1.12"` between `"1.11"` and `"2.0"`. `pre-install-commands` now passes
`{matrix:dbt}` as a third arg. |
| `scripts/test/pre-install-airflow.sh` | `$3=DBT_VERSION` is now
**required** (no default). Selects
`requirements-airflow-${AIRFLOW}-dbt-${DBT}.txt`; for a missing **1.11
or 1.12** lockfile this now **hard-fails** (`::error::`) rather than
silently substituting — every supported Airflow version is expected to
have both. Other dbt minors (1.5-1.10, 2.0) still fall back to the
dbt-1.11 baseline with a `::warning::`, since jobs that need them
(dbt-1-5-4, dbt-async, dbtf, performance, telemetry,
integration-expensive) either re-pin dbt in their own setup step
afterward or rely on this baseline directly. The dbt version-check now
uses the working `installed:` parser. |
|
`requirements/requirements-airflow-{2.9,2.10,2.11,3.0,3.1,3.2,3.3}-dbt-1.12.txt`
| **New** — 7 pinned lockfiles for `dbt-core==1.12.0` (stable),
generated in `python:3.10` linux/amd64 Docker. |
| `.github/workflows/test-unprivileged.yml` | `Run-Unit-Tests` matrix
`dbt-version: ["1.10"] → ["1.11", "1.12"]` (additive, not a replace —
see below). (This job lived in `test.yml` when this PR started; it has
since moved to the new unprivileged workflow as part of an unrelated CI
split on `main` — the dbt-version bump now applies there instead.) |
| `.github/workflows/test.yml` | `Run-Integration-Tests` matrix
`dbt-version: ["1.11"] → ["1.12"]` (integration coverage moved off 1.11
entirely, see below). Airflow `3.3` (added on `main` after this PR was
opened) is preserved in the merged matrix. |
| `tests/dbt/test_runner.py` |
`test_handle_exception_if_needed_after_exception` now picks the expected
missing-package error text by the **installed** dbt major/minor (`<=
1.11` keeps the old wording, else dbt 1.12's reworded one), so the test
passes whichever dbt lockfile a job installs — including jobs that fall
back to the dbt-1.11 baseline. |
| `docs/policy/compatibility-policy.rst` | Added `1.12` to the dbt Core
supported-versions line. |

## dbt-core: beta → stable

The branch originally pinned `dbt-core==1.12.0b2` (the only build
available at the time). **dbt-core 1.12.0 has since shipped stable on
PyPI**, so all 6 lockfiles were regenerated against it:

- Per file: installed the existing (beta) lockfile in a fresh
`python:3.10` linux/amd64 container, then `uv pip install -P dbt-core
"dbt-core==1.12.0"` (upgrades only `dbt-core` and whatever it strictly
requires — every other pin is untouched), then `uv pip freeze`.
- Diff per file is exactly 3 lines: `dbt-core` `1.12.0b2 → 1.12.0`,
`dbt-core-experimental-parser` `2.0.0a1 → 2.0.0a4`, `dbt-adapters`
`1.24.2 → 1.24.5`.
- `uv pip check` clean on all 6 files.
- `dbt-postgres`/`dbt-bigquery` are no longer pre-release builds either
(they resolved to stable versions compatible with dbt-core 1.12.0 during
the regenerate) — the "Residual TODOs" item about pre-release adapter
pins from the original PR body no longer applies.

## Integration coverage: dropped 1.11, moved fully to 1.12 — unit tests
keep both

A later commit on this branch (`Move integration tests to dbt 1.12 and
assert dbt 1.12 error wording`) changed `Run-Integration-Tests`'s
`dbt-version` from `["1.11", "1.12"]` to `["1.12"]` only — integration
coverage moves to 1.12 rather than running both.

`Run-Unit-Tests` initially followed the same pattern (`1.10` → `1.12`,
replace not additive). Tatiana's review pointed out that testing units
only against the newest dbt drops coverage of the more broadly-used 1.11
line, so it's now `dbt-version: ["1.11", "1.12"]` (additive) — unit
tests run both, integration runs only 1.12. This roughly doubles the
`Run-Unit-Tests` matrix (up to 56 cells before exclusions instead of
28), which is the direct cost of that broader coverage.

## Base-image pip/wheel pin bug (fixed on this branch)

An early pass at generating the lockfiles picked up the
`python:3.10-slim` base image's bootstrap `pip==23.0.1`/`wheel==0.45.1`
in the freeze. That `pip` downgrade broke py3.12/3.13 (`AttributeError:
module 'pkgutil' has no attribute 'ImpImporter'`, removed in 3.12).
Fixed by stripping those two pins from all 6 files, matching the
dbt-1.11 lockfiles which don't pin them either. (This fix carried
through the beta→stable regeneration — the regenerated files were built
from the already-fixed lockfiles, and `uv pip freeze` doesn't
reintroduce base-image pins since it only freezes the venv.)

## Rebase onto `main`

This branch was rebased onto current `main` (which independently landed
Airflow 3.3 support and split `test.yml` into `test.yml`
(secret-dependent jobs) + `test-unprivileged.yml`
(`Type-Check`/`Run-Unit-Tests`/telemetry/performance, gated on plain
`pull_request` instead of `pull_request_target`)). Conflicts were
resolved by union-ing both sides' matrix changes (Airflow 3.3 + dbt
1.12) rather than dropping either, and by re-homing the unit-test
dbt-version bump into `test-unprivileged.yml` since that's where
`Run-Unit-Tests` now lives.

## Airflow 3.3 × dbt 1.12: added the missing lockfile (Copilot catch)

Because Airflow 3.3 landed on `main` after this branch's original 6
dbt-1.12 lockfiles were generated, there was no
`requirements-airflow-3.3-dbt-1.12.txt` — Copilot's review correctly
flagged that the `airflow-version: 3.3` cells in both matrices were
labeled `dbt-version: 1.12` but `pre-install-airflow.sh`'s fallback
would silently install dbt 1.11 instead, so those cells would have
passed while mislabeled. Added `requirements-airflow-3.3-dbt-1.12.txt`
the same way as the other 6 (installed the existing 3.3-dbt-1.11
lockfile, then moved `dbt-core` to `1.12.0` and let `dbt-databricks`
move with it via `uv pip install -P dbt-core -P dbt-databricks`, since
the 1.11 file's `dbt-databricks==1.12.2` caps `dbt-core<1.11.13`;
stripped the same base-image `wheel` pin the other files had removed).
`uv pip check` clean; installed dbt-core resolves to `1.12.0`. All 7
airflow versions now have a real dbt-1.12 lockfile — the fallback path
is no longer hit in the normal matrix, but `pre-install-airflow.sh` now
logs a `::warning::` if a future (airflow, dbt) gap like this one ever
recurs.

## Hard-fail on a missing 1.11/1.12 lockfile (Tatiana)

Tatiana flagged that `pre-install-airflow.sh`'s silent
fallback-to-dbt-1.11 masked real gaps: once the dbt-version assertion
actually worked (fixed earlier on this branch), the fallback just
reassigned "expected" to match whatever got installed, so a missing
lockfile silently passed instead of failing. Scoped the fix narrowly to
this PR's actual concern rather than reverting the fallback wholesale: a
missing **1.11 or 1.12** lockfile now hard-fails with `::error::` (every
one of the 7 Airflow versions is expected to have both), while other dbt
minors (1.5-1.10, 2.0) keep the silent fallback + warning, since their
jobs either re-pin dbt themselves afterward or rely on this baseline
directly and a blanket hard-fail would break hatch env creation for all
of them before any re-pin step could run.

**Still open:** Tatiana followed up suggesting we go further — fail (and
generate a real lockfile) for *every* missing `(airflow, dbt)` pair, not
just 1.11/1.12, rather than falling back at all. Investigated this:
`uv`'s strict resolver genuinely can't produce a coherent env for some
old-dbt + new-Airflow combos (e.g. dbt 1.5 + Airflow 3.0 conflict on
`jinja2`), which is presumably why the job-specific `*-setup.sh` re-pin
scripts use permissive plain `pip install` rather than `uv`. Generating
real lockfiles for the full `1.5-2.0 × 7-Airflow-version` matrix (or
switching that install path to plain `pip`) is a bigger undertaking than
this PR's scope. Filed astronomer/astronomer-cosmos#2902 to track
raising the minimum supported dbt-core version instead, which would
shrink/eliminate the problem by dropping the oldest, most conflict-prone
dbt minors — left open for discussion there rather than attempted in
this PR.

## ⚠️ Reviewer attention: 2.9 / 3.1 lockfile footprint

The hand-curated `dbt-1.11` lockfiles for **Airflow 2.9 and 3.1**
omitted the `google-cloud-*` / full `dbt-bigquery` dependency tree (a
conflict-avoidance workaround). With dbt-1.12's adapter set that tree
now resolves cleanly (`uv pip check` passes), so the `2.9`/`3.1`
dbt-1.12 files **include it** (+~95 lines each). This is **new
coverage** — the curated dbt-1.11 files are untouched and still serve
the fallback path — but the `2.9×1.12` / `3.1×1.12` cells should be
watched on the first CI run for any runtime aiobotocore/google issues
that `uv pip check` can't see. The other four files (2.10/2.11/3.0/3.2)
are minimal dbt-stack-only diffs.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI unit tests pass on dbt-1.12 across the Python × Airflow matrix
(via `test-unprivileged.yml`).
- [ ] CI integration tests pass on dbt-1.12 (`test.yml`, integration
fully moved off 1.11).
- [ ] 2.9×1.12 and 3.1×1.12 cells pass (the expanded-footprint files).
- [ ] Pre-existing jobs (async / dbtf / loom / kubernetes / expensive /
telemetry / perf) unaffected — they fall back to the dbt-1.11 baseline
as before.
- [ ] Airflow 3.3 × dbt 1.12 cells now install the real 1.12 lockfile
(no fallback warning in the logs).

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Touchpoint table matches the diff.
- [ ] Agree with unit tests keeping both 1.11 and 1.12 while integration
moves fully to 1.12 (see coverage section above).
- [ ] Weigh in on the still-open "fail instead of dynamically installing
older dbt" discussion (see hard-fail section above /
astronomer/astronomer-cosmos#2902).
- [ ] 2.9/3.1 footprint expansion accepted (see callout above).
- [ ] CI green → ready to mark non-draft.

v2.9.0

Summary

This release updates the default lychee version from v0.23.0 to v0.24.2.

The main reason for this release is compatibility with the new lychee 0.24.x release artifacts. Starting with lychee v0.24.0, the archive layout changed, and the lychee binary may now be packaged inside a subdirectory. lychee-action now detects that layout automatically, so users can upgrade without changing their workflows.

If you use:

uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2

you will get the new version once the floating v2 tag has been updated. If you pin exact versions, update to:

uses: lycheeverse/u8681f91d9023c340@users.invalid

What’s new from lychee v0.24.x

Better diagnostics

lychee now reports line and column numbers for detected links. This makes broken link reports easier to act on, especially in larger documentation sites or generated reports.

Text fragment checking

lychee can now check URL text fragments, such as links containing #:~:text=.... This helps catch links that point to a valid page but no longer points to the intended highlighted text.

Sitemap support

lychee can now read sitemap.xml inputs. This is useful for checking published websites or generated documentation sites where the sitemap is the easiest source of URLs to validate.

JUnit output

lychee now supports JUnit output. This makes it easier to integrate link checking results with CI systems and test reporting tools that understand JUnit XML.

Redirect and remap visibility

lychee can now show redirects and remaps more clearly. This helps explain why a URL was checked as a different final URL and makes debugging link-checking behavior easier.

Multiple config files

lychee now supports multiple configuration files and expanded config handling. This is useful for repositories that split documentation, website, or package-specific link-checking settings.

Timeout handling

lychee can now accept timeouts explicitly. This gives users more control over how strict their link checks should be for flaky or slow endpoints.

subject: Avoid deprecated `airflow.exceptions.AirflowSkipException` import on Airflow 3.1+ (#2796)
message:
Avoid deprecated `airflow.exceptions.AirflowSkipException` import on Airflow 3.1+ (#2796)

## Problem

On Airflow 3.2+, importing `AirflowSkipException` from
`airflow.exceptions` is deprecated and emits a `UserWarning` at import
time:

```
WARNING - airflow.exceptions.AirflowSkipException is deprecated and will be removed in a future
version. Use airflow.sdk.exceptions.AirflowSkipException instead. category=UserWarning
```

Cosmos imports it from `airflow.exceptions` in `local.py`, `watcher.py`,
`_watcher/base.py`, and `_k8s_common.py`, so the warning shows up at DAG
parse / task execution.

## Fix

`airflow.sdk.exceptions.AirflowSkipException` only exists on Airflow
3.2+ — the Task SDK does not expose it on Airflow 2 / 3.0 / 3.1, where
`airflow.exceptions.AirflowSkipException` is **not** deprecated. So a
plain switch would break older versions.

Add a version-tolerant re-export in the existing
`cosmos/airflow/compatibility.py` (which already centralises Airflow 2/3
import differences) that prefers the Task SDK path and falls back to
`airflow.exceptions`, and import `AirflowSkipException` from there in
the operator modules. `AirflowException` is unaffected (not deprecated)
and is left as-is.

## Verification

- **Airflow 3.2.0**: importing the Cosmos operators emits **no**
`AirflowSkipException` deprecation warning; it resolves to
`airflow.sdk.exceptions.AirflowSkipException`.
- **Airflow 3.0 / 3.1**: the Task SDK does not expose
`AirflowSkipException`, so it falls back to
`airflow.exceptions.AirflowSkipException` (which is not deprecated
there, so no warning).
- New regression test (`tests/airflow/test_compatibility.py`) asserts
the shim resolves to the Task SDK on Airflow ≥ 3.2 and to
`airflow.exceptions` below it.

subject: Fix mypy no-any-return error in `_resolve_env_var` (#2904)
message:
Fix mypy no-any-return error in `_resolve_env_var` (#2904)

## Description

mypy 2.2.0 flags a new error that fails the Type-Check job on the
Dependabot bump of `mirrors-mypy` to v2.2.0 (#2897):

```
cosmos/dbt/project.py:62: error: Returning Any from function declared to return "str"  [no-any-return]
```

`jinja2.Template.render()` resolves to `Any` in the pre-commit mypy
environment, so `_resolve_env_var` was returning `Any` from a function
declared to return `str`. This annotates the intermediate variable as
`str`, making the return type explicit. No runtime behaviour change.

## Verification

Ran the Type-Check command (`pre-commit run mypy`) locally against both

subject: Preserve container ENTRYPOINT by default in Kubernetes-based dbt operators (#2891)
message:
Preserve container ENTRYPOINT by default in Kubernetes-based dbt operators (#2891)

## Description

`build_kube_args` unconditionally split the dbt command into
`cmds=["dbt"]` and `arguments=[...]`. Setting `cmds` on a
`KubernetesPodOperator`/`GKEStartPodOperator` populates the pod
container's `command` field, which overrides the container image's
`ENTRYPOINT`. Images that rely on their `ENTRYPOINT` to perform setup
before `dbt` starts, such as sourcing secrets injected by a sidecar
(e.g. a Vault agent writing `/vault/secrets/config`), lose that setup
and `dbt` fails with the expected environment variables missing.

This affects `ExecutionMode.KUBERNETES`, `WATCHER_KUBERNETES`,
`AWS_EKS`, and `GCP_GKE` / `WATCHER_GCP_GKE`, since they all share
`_k8s_common.build_kube_args`.

Reproduced end-to-end against a local kind cluster with a minimal image
whose `ENTRYPOINT` sets an env var before exec'ing a stub `dbt`: before
this change the pod spec has `command: ["dbt"]`, the entrypoint never
runs, and the stub fails with the env var unset; after this change
`command` is left empty, the entrypoint runs, and the stub succeeds.

`cmds` is now left untouched by default, so the full dbt command
(including the executable) is passed as `arguments` and the image's
`ENTRYPOINT` is preserved, restoring the pre-1.15.0 behavior. A
user-supplied `cmds` (for example a custom entrypoint or wrapper set via
`operator_args`) is preserved exactly as provided, with the full dbt
command passed as `arguments`. The executable is stripped from
`arguments` only when `cmds` is already set to `["dbt"]`, to avoid
running `dbt dbt ...`.

## Related Issue(s)

closes https://github.com/astronomer/astronomer-cosmos/issues/2889
closes BOSS-561

## Breaking Change?

No.

subject: Proposal for introducing a Snowflake dbt Project execution mode (#2896)
message:
Proposal for introducing a Snowflake dbt Project execution mode (#2896)

## Description

This PR adds a request-for-comments proposal for experimental support
for running
Snowflake dbt Project objects through Cosmos while preserving Airflow's
Model-level task graph and observability.

This PR is proposal-only. It does not implement the execution mode or
change any
runtime behaviour.

The proposed design:

- renders the Airflow graph from an exact-snapshot manifest fetched from
  Snowflake using `manifest_conn_id`;
- submits one remote `EXECUTE DBT PROJECT ... build` command;
- projects model and test progress into watcher-compatible Airflow tasks
using
  Snowflake telemetry;
- uses deterministic query tags for recovery without duplicate
execution; and
- introduces the mode experimentally through validation and
implementation
  phases.

The proposal explicitly records the required Cosmos contract changes and
keeps
them scoped to the new execution mode. It also identifies several ship
gates
that requires validation against a live Snowflake account, particularly
the project
version selection, telemetry semantics, crash recovery, and
cross-orchestrator
concurrency.

The main areas where feedback would be especially valuable are:

1. Whether the proposed rendering and execution configuration is
appropriate.
2. Whether Snowflake telemetry is sufficiently stable for model-level
state.
3. Whether the recovery and concurrency safeguards are adequate.
4. Whether the identified compatibility boundaries protect existing
Cosmos DAGs and execution modes.

Full proposal: [Support dbt Projects on Snowflake as a Cosmos execution
mode](plans/001-snow-dbt-project.md)

## Related Issue(s)

No related issue yet. This proposal PR is intended to host the initial
design
discussion.

## Breaking Change?

No. This PR adds documentation only and does not change runtime or
public API
behavior.

A future implementation would require the mode-scoped contract changes
recorded
in the proposal. Those changes must be covered by regression tests to
preserve
the behaviour of existing execution modes and DAGs.

subject: Add Python 3.14 to test matrix (Airflow 3.2/3.3, dbt-1.12 only) (#2903)
message:
Add Python 3.14 to test matrix (Airflow 3.2/3.3, dbt-1.12 only) (#2903)

## Summary

Adds Python 3.14 to the test matrix, scoped to Airflow 3.2/3.3 with
dbt-1.12 only (dbt-1.11 has no Python 3.14 classifier on PyPI, and older
Airflow versions weren't attempted). This picks up where #2537 left off
— that PR was closed because dbt-core didn't support Python 3.14 at the
time; dbt-core 1.12.0 has since added the classifier.

## Why the lockfiles needed more than a flat version bump

The `requirements/requirements-airflow-X.Y-dbt-Z.txt` lockfiles are
exact-pin freezes shared across **all** Python versions for a given
(airflow, dbt) pair — there's no per-Python lockfile. Adding 3.14 as a
new axis value surfaced two real problems:

1. **`ray` / `scipy`** — straightforward: the pinned versions have no
cp314 wheels, and newer releases that add cp314 support do exist, so
these are marker-gated (`python_version >= "3.14"`) bumps in
`requirements-airflow-3.2-dbt-1.12.txt`.
2. **A real upstream standoff** — `apache-airflow-providers-amazon`
requires `redshift_connector>=2.1.13` specifically when `python_version
>= "3.14"` (confirmed present in every recent release, including the
latest 9.32.0). Satisfying that forces
`boto3`→`botocore`→`aiobotocore`→`s3fs`→`fsspec`→`gcsfs` upward, and
every `gcsfs` version compatible with that chain requires
`google-cloud-storage>=3.7+` — but `dbt-bigquery`, even at its latest
1.12.0 release, caps `google-cloud-storage<3.2`. No package-version bump
on either side resolves this today.

The fix: pin `apache-airflow-providers-amazon==9.24.0` for
`python_version >= "3.14"` in `requirements-airflow-3.3-dbt-1.12.txt` —
the last release before the Python-3.14-conditional `redshift_connector`
floor was added — which sidesteps the cascade entirely without touching
`dbt-bigquery`/`gcsfs`. Paired with a marker-gated `scipy` bump for the
same reason as above.

All four changed lockfile lines were verified locally (via `uv pip
install -r ... --python <interpreter>`) to install cleanly under
**both** Python 3.10 and Python 3.14 from the same file, so the existing
3.10–3.13 install path is unaffected.

## Residual risk to watch on first CI run

`lxml==5.4.0` (in the 3.2 lockfile) has no cp314 wheel and wasn't bumped
past 6.0, since doing so would re-trigger the `redshift-connector`
cascade above (it caps `lxml<6.0.0`). It'll build from source under
Python 3.14 in CI instead — this succeeded locally, but I couldn't
confirm GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runners have
`libxml2-dev`/`libxslt-dev` preinstalled.

## Touchpoints

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` | 3.14 classifier + hatch `tests` matrix |
| `.github/workflows/test.yml`,
`.github/workflows/test-unprivileged.yml` | 3.14 added to the Python
matrix, excluded for every Airflow version except 3.2/3.3 (and dbt-1.11,
in the unit-test job) |
| `requirements/requirements-airflow-3.2-dbt-1.12.txt`,
`requirements/requirements-airflow-3.3-dbt-1.12.txt` | Marker-gated pin
bumps described above |
| `docs/policy/compatibility-policy.rst`, `AGENTS.md` |
Supported-versions docs |

## Test plan

- [ ] CI unit tests pass on Python 3.14 × Airflow {3.2, 3.3} × dbt 1.12.
- [ ] CI integration tests pass on the same cells.
- [ ] Watch the `lxml` sdist build on the 3.2 cell for missing system
headers.
- [ ] Confirm no other Python-version cells regressed (exclude list
should leave 3.10–3.13 behavior untouched).

subject: Keep the Airflow DAGs folder out of dbt's plugin discovery path (#2893)
message:
Keep the Airflow DAGs folder out of dbt's plugin discovery path (#2893)

## Description

dbt-core discovers plugins by importing every importable top-level
module whose name starts with `dbt_`
(`dbt.plugins.manager._get_dbt_modules` scans the whole `sys.path` via
`pkgutil.iter_modules`). Airflow puts its DAGs folder on the path, so
when Cosmos runs dbt (the in-process `dbtRunner` is the default for
`LoadMode.DBT_LS` since Cosmos 1.9), dbt's plugin discovery imports any
DAG file named `dbt_*.py` as a side effect. That:

* leaks and duplicates DAGs across unrelated Cosmos DAGs when running
in-process (`AirflowDagDuplicatedIdException`), and
* crashes the dbt command in subprocess mode, since the imported DAG
file re-initializes Airflow.

This adds two helpers in `cosmos/dbt/project.py` that keep the DAGs
folder out of dbt's reach, scoped to the dbt invocation only (installed
dbt plugins, which live in site-packages rather than the DAGs folder,
are untouched):

* `exclude_dags_folder_from_sys_path` strips the DAGs folder from the
live `sys.path` around in-process `dbtRunner` calls
(`cosmos/dbt/runner.py`).
* `remove_dags_folder_from_pythonpath` strips it from the `PYTHONPATH`
passed to dbt subprocesses, both at parse time (`cosmos/dbt/graph.py`)
and at task execution time (`cosmos/operators/local.py`).

Both resolve the DAGs folder via `airflow.settings.DAGS_FOLDER`,
applying `os.path.realpath` to it and to each path entry so relative and
absolute forms compare consistently.

### Opt-out config

The handling is gated behind a new
`enable_dags_folder_exclusion_from_dbt` config (default `True`, env var
`AIRFLOW__COSMOS__ENABLE_DAGS_FOLDER_EXCLUSION_FROM_DBT`). Because
stripping the DAGs folder means a genuine dbt plugin named `dbt_*`
placed inside the DAGs folder would no longer be discovered, users who
rely on that can set the config to `False` to restore the previous
behaviour. Documented in `docs/reference/configs/cosmos-conf.rst`.

### Note on Astro Cloud

I could reliably reproduce this bug locally (`astro dev`), but not on an
actual Astro Cloud deployment. Astro's DAG-bundle layout nests the
actual DAG files a level deeper than a `DAGS_FOLDER`-based setup, and
Airflow 3's bundle mechanism appends the bundle root rather than that
nested `dags/` folder, so dbt's plugin scan never sees the sibling
`dbt_*.py` file as a top-level importable module. This fix, keyed off
`DAGS_FOLDER`, addresses classic/local setups; Cloud's bundle-based
deploys are structurally unaffected by this specific leak path for a
different, unrelated reason.

### Testing

Reproduced the leak locally with two DAGs (a `dbt_*`-prefixed
"infectious" file and a plain `DbtDag` "victim" file), confirming both
symptoms before the fix and their absence after. Added functional tests
that drive real dbt through the actual Cosmos entry points, one per
invocation mode: the in-process `dbtRunner` path via `run_command` and
the subprocess path via `run_command_with_subprocess`. Each drops a
`dbt_*.py` file in the DAGs folder and asserts real dbt imports it when
the exclusion is disabled and skips it when enabled. Also added unit
tests for the helpers themselves (`sys.path`/`PYTHONPATH` manipulation,
relative-path resolution, and the flag-off no-op behaviour).

## Related Issue(s)

closes #1673
Closes BOSS-233

## Breaking Change?

The DAGs-folder exclusion is enabled by default. A dbt plugin named
`dbt_*` living inside the Airflow DAGs folder will no longer be
auto-discovered while enabled; set
`enable_dags_folder_exclusion_from_dbt=False` to opt out.

subject: Support lists of paths for ProjectConfig relative-path args (#2875)
message: Support lists of paths for ProjectConfig relative-path args (#2875) ## Summary - `ProjectConfig` now accepts `models_relative_paths`/`seeds_relative_paths`/`snapshots_relative_paths` (a single path or a list), mirroring dbt's own support for multiple `model-paths`/`seed-paths`/`snapshot-paths`. - The old singular `models_relative_path`/`seeds_relative_path`/`snapshots_relative_path` args and the derived `models_path`/`seeds_path`/`snapshots_path` attributes still work but now raise a `DeprecationWarning` and will be removed in Cosmos 2.0. - Extended the deprecated `LoadMode.CUSTOM` legacy parser (`LegacyDbtProject`) to crawl multiple model/seed/snapshot directories instead of assuming a single one; also fixed a pre-existing gap where `dbt_snapshots_dir` was never passed through to it. - `ProjectConfig.validate_project()` now validates every configured model directory instead of just the first one. Follow-up fixes from review: - Fixed a shared mutable list default on `ProjectConfig.models_paths`/`seeds_paths`/`snapshots_paths` that could leak state across instances created without `dbt_project_path`. - Fixed `LoadMode.CUSTOM` silently dropping models under nested `models_relative_paths` (e.g. `"custom/models"`) by preserving the full relative path instead of just `Path.stem`. - Fixed `LegacyDbtProject` misclassifying (and crashing on) a snapshots dir nested inside a models dir, by using proper path containment instead of a substring check. closes: https://github.com/astronomer/astronomer-cosmos/issues/2100 closes: BOSS-197 ## Test plan - [x] `hatch run tests.py3.11-2.10-1.9:test tests/test_config.py tests/dbt/parser/test_project.py tests/dbt/test_graph.py` - [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` (ruff, black, mypy) - [x] CI DagRun --------- Co-authored-by: Copilot Autofix powered by AI <175728472+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com> Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5

subject: Document verified Cosmos/Runtime/dbt Core compatibility (#2914)
message:
Document verified Cosmos/Runtime/dbt Core compatibility (#2914)

## Description

Adds three empirically-verified compatibility tables to
`docs/policy/compatibility-policy.rst`, replacing/supplementing the
previously declared-only version ranges:

- **Verified Python × dbt Core support** — each dbt Core release from
1.5 to 2.0 pip-installed into plain Python 3.10–3.14 images and
import-checked. Surfaces two real breakages: dbt Core 1.5–1.7 fail on
Python 3.12+ (`distutils` removal), and 1.8–1.11 fail on Python 3.14
(`mashumaro` incompatibility). dbt Fusion (2.0) isn't pip-installable as
`dbt-core` at all.
- **Astronomer Runtime** table simplified to Runtime series → Airflow →
Python, cross-linked to the dbt Core table, with a note pointing readers
to each package's PyPI page for the live, authoritative Python-support
metadata.
- **Cosmos and Astronomer Runtime compatibility (verified)** — every
Cosmos release from 1.5.1 to 1.15.0 pip-installed into the official
Runtime Docker image for each Runtime series (11, 12, 13, 3.0, 3.1, 3.2,
3.3), then checked via `airflow plugins` (the real plugin-loading path,
not a bare import). Documents exactly which Cosmos releases work on
which Runtime series, with root-cause tracebacks for each failure mode
(including a severe one: Cosmos 1.6.0–1.13.1 crash the entire `airflow`
process, not just plugin loading, on Airflow 3.2/3.3).

### Follow-up fixes from Copilot review

- Replaced a dangling "existing Runtime 3.0 compatibility note"
reference with a real `:doc:` link to
`docs/policy/airflow3-compatibility.rst`, which documents the actual
constraint (Cosmos's AF3 plugin requires Airflow >= 3.1).
- Joined an inline literal that spanned a line break (the `distutils`
exception text) onto a single line.
- Corrected a `list-table` cell's indentation. Note: Copilot Autofix had
already applied a fix for this finding directly to the branch, but that
fix introduced a *different* misalignment (6-space indent vs. the
table's consistent 5-space); this PR's version corrects it properly.

[BOSS-571](https://linear.app/astronomer/issue/BOSS-571/version-compatibility-matrix-published-and-linked-from-the-cosmos-docs)

closes: BOSS-571

No — documentation only.

subject: Group github/codeql-action updates in a single Dependabot PR (#2928)
message:
Group github/codeql-action updates in a single Dependabot PR (#2928)

## Summary

Group `github/codeql-action*` updates into a single Dependabot PR.

CodeQL requires the `init` and `analyze` actions to run the **same**
version. Dependabot was opening `github/codeql-action/init` and
`github/codeql-action/analyze` as **separate** PRs, so each branch ended
up with a version-skewed init/analyze pair and failed the `Analyze
(actions)` / `Analyze (python)` jobs. This has recurred every codeql
release, e.g. #2922 + #2925 (4.37.2) this week and #2912 + #2913
(4.37.1) last week.

## Fix

Add a `codeql-action` group to the `github-actions` ecosystem so both
sub-actions bump together in one PR that lands at a single, consistent
version and passes CI.

```yaml
groups:
  codeql-action:
    patterns:
      - "github/codeql-action*"
```

No change to cooldown, schedule, labels, or reviewers.

subject: Fix flaky `source_pruning_dag` integration test (AF 3.0) by seeding first (#2927)
message:
Fix flaky `source_pruning_dag` integration test (AF 3.0) by seeding first (#2927)

Fixes the intermittent red on the Airflow 3.0 integration job
(`Run-Integration-Tests (*, 3.0, 1.12, 2)`), where
`test_example_dag[source_pruning_dag]` fails with `relation
"public.raw_orders" does not exist`.

Failing runs:
-
https://github.com/astronomer/astronomer-cosmos/actions/runs/30292424750
(main, after #2875)
-
https://github.com/astronomer/astronomer-cosmos/actions/runs/30335826612/job/90200397105?pr=2923
(#2923)

## Root cause

`source_pruning_dag`'s `raw_orders` source has a freshness check that
queries its source table. That table is produced by the `raw_orders`
seed, but a dbt source has no dependency on a seed, so nothing orders
the seed before the freshness task. On Airflow 3.0's `dag.test()` the
source can run first — before the table exists — so it fails. It's
intermittent (only AF 3.0's task ordering triggers it), which is why
unrelated PRs go red.

## Fix

Make the test self-contained: a `seeded_altered_jaffle_shop` fixture
runs `dbt deps` + `dbt seed` before the DAG, so the source table exists
regardless of task order. `source_pruning_dag` stays out of the generic
unordered parametrization. Test-only change.

## Verification

Passes locally on Python 3.10 / Airflow 3.0 / dbt 1.12 against a real
Postgres:
`hatch run tests.py3.10-3.0-1.12:test-integration
tests/test_example_dags.py::test_source_pruning_dag` → `1 passed`.

docs: reference stable Cosmos 1.11.0 for dbt Fusion instead of the 1.11.0a1 alpha (#2861)

## Problem

The dbt Fusion guide (`docs/guides/dbt_setup/dbt-fusion.rst`) still
points users at the `1.11.0a1` alpha and `pip install astronomer-cosmos
--pre`. dbt Fusion support has since shipped in the **stable 1.11.0**
release (Cosmos is now at 1.14.2), so these references are stale and
steer users to install a pre-release unnecessarily.

## Fix

subject: Emit per-model outlets in `ExecutionMode.WATCHER_KUBERNETES` (#2595)
message:
Emit per-model outlets in `ExecutionMode.WATCHER_KUBERNETES` (#2595)

## Summary

Cosmos 1.14.0 added per-model outlet URI emission to
`ExecutionMode.WATCHER`
consumer sensors, but the `WATCHER_KUBERNETES` path never wired up the
producer's log-parsing callback with the `model_outlet_uris` /
`dataset_namespace` bindings that the SUBPROCESS and DBT_RUNNER paths
use.
As a result, the per-node `*_status` XCom dict always carried
`"outlet_uris": []`, and the Kubernetes consumer sensors had no way to
emit
Airflow Assets — so lineage catalogs that read from Airflow's outlet
system
(OpenLineage, OpenMetadata, etc.) showed pipelines with empty
inputs/outputs
and no table-level edges for WATCHER_KUBERNETES-mode runs.

## Changes

### Producer side

`DbtProducerWatcherKubernetesOperator`:
- Accepts `manifest_filepath` (already threaded through `task_args` from
  `ProjectConfig.manifest_path` by `cosmos.converter`).
- At `execute` time, resolves the dataset namespace from the profile and
  populates `self._model_outlet_uris` by reading the scheduler-side
manifest. The pod's own `target/manifest.json` isn't reachable from the
scheduler, so the SUBPROCESS watcher's `project_dir`-based lookup can't
  be reused here — we read the manifest Cosmos already parses for DAG
  rendering instead.
- Publishes both values into module-level globals alongside the existing
  `producer_task_context`, so the static `WatcherKubernetesCallback` can
  thread them through to `store_dbt_resource_status_from_log`.

### Consumer side

`DbtConsumerWatcherKubernetesSensor` now overrides `execute` and
`execute_complete` to call a new `_emit_datasets` method, mirroring
`DbtConsumerWatcherSensor`. `execute_complete` extracts `outlet_uris`
from
the trigger event before emitting.

### Shared helper

`LocalDbtBaseOperator.register_dataset`'s body is extracted into a new
`cosmos.dataset.register_dataset_on_task` free function so both
execution
modes can use it without inheriting from the local operator. The local
method becomes a thin delegate; its public signature and behaviour are
preserved.

## Backwards compatibility

No breaking changes. When `manifest_filepath` is not supplied or the
manifest file isn't present on the scheduler, the producer logs a
warning
and skips outlet population — same graceful degradation as the
SUBPROCESS
watcher when `{project_dir}/target/manifest.json` is absent. dbt
execution
and XCom status reporting continue to work in that case; only dataset
emission is lost.

## Test plan

New unit tests under `tests/operators/test_watcher_kubernetes_unit.py`:

- [x] Producer `execute` resolves namespace + populates
`_model_outlet_uris` from the manifest
- [x] Producer `execute` publishes outlets/namespace/context into module
globals
- [x] Producer `execute` silently skips outlet population when manifest
is missing
- [x] `WatcherKubernetesCallback.progress_callback` passes outlet state
into `store_dbt_resource_status_from_log`
- [x] Consumer `_emit_datasets` registers one Asset per outlet URI
- [x] Consumer `_emit_datasets` no-ops when `emit_datasets=False` or
`_outlet_uris=[]`
- [x] Consumer `execute_complete` stashes `outlet_uris` from the trigger
event before emitting

An `autouse` fixture resets the module-level producer globals between
tests so state doesn't leak.

## Context for review

Found this gap while setting up OpenMetadata ingestion for a
`WATCHER_KUBERNETES` deployment: Airflow pipelines showed up in OM but
had empty inputs/outputs, so no table-level lineage edges were drawn.
Traced it to the producer callback not threading outlet bindings through
— a regression-adjacent gap from Cosmos 1.14.0, where WATCHER got outlet
support but WATCHER_KUBERNETES didn't. Code change above mirrors the
SUBPROCESS path as closely as possible.

subject: Make partial-parse cache reads resilient to NFS ESTALE races (#2867)
message:
Make partial-parse cache reads resilient to NFS ESTALE races (#2867)

## Description

Follow-up to #2815 (atomic `partial_parse.msgpack` cache writes).

After #2815 switched the partial-parse cache writes to `safe_copy`
(write to a temp file, then `os.replace`), we started seeing tasks
**crash** on a shared network filesystem (NFS/EFS) when the cache is
written concurrently:

```
OSError: [Errno 116] Stale file handle:
  '.../cosmos/<dag>/target/partial_parse.msgpack' -> '/tmp/.../target/tmpXXXX'
  File ".../cosmos/cache.py", line 323, in _copy_partial_parse_to_project
  File ".../cosmos/fs.py", line 53, in safe_copy
  File ".../shutil.py", line 273, in copyfile   # _fastcopy_sendfile
```

### Root cause

`safe_copy` publishes via `os.replace` (rename), which unlinks the
previous inode. When a **reader** task is mid-`shutil.copyfile` on the
shared source (`partial_parse.msgpack` / `manifest.json`) and a
**writer** task atomically replaces it, the reader's open handle is
invalidated. The POSIX guarantee that "an open reader keeps the old,
now-anonymous inode alive" holds on a local filesystem but **not across
NFS clients**, so the reader gets `ESTALE` instead of a consistent read
— and the task fails.

In other words, #2815 correctly removed the *torn read* (previously
surfaced as a caught `ValueError` from `msgpack.unpack` and silently
degraded to a full parse), but on NFS it traded that for an **uncaught
`ESTALE` that crashes the task**.

### Change

Partial parse is a pure optimisation, so the fix restores the pre-#2815
behaviour: absorb the copy race **at the cache layer and fall back to a
full `dbt` parse**, in the same place the torn read was already
tolerated (`_copy_partial_parse_to_project`, right next to
`patch_partial_parse_content`'s `ValueError` catch).

- **`cosmos/cache.py`** — wrap the partial-parse copy in `try/except
OSError` and fall back to a full parse instead of failing the task. The
log level is split by cause: transient `ESTALE` (a concurrent task
atomically replaced the source mid-copy on a shared FS) logs at `info`;
any other `OSError` (e.g. `EACCES` on a misconfigured `cache_dir`,
`ENOSPC`) logs at `warning` so a persistent problem that silently
disables partial parse stays visible.
- **`cosmos/operators/local.py` and `cosmos/fs.py` are unchanged** — the
critical operator execute path is untouched, and `safe_copy` stays
as-is.

Tests move the fallback coverage to `tests/test_cache.py` (parametrised:
`ESTALE` → `info`, `EACCES` → `warning`), verifying the copy race is
swallowed and never raises.

### Notes for reviewers (anticipated questions)

- **Why catch `OSError` broadly?** Partial parse must never fail the
task. Narrowing the catch to only `ESTALE` would turn an unrelated,
recoverable-by-full-parse error (e.g. a transient cache-dir permission
blip) into a hard task failure. Instead we keep the broad catch but
raise the log level for non-transient causes so real misconfigurations
are not swallowed silently.
- **Why not retry `safe_copy` on `ESTALE`?** An earlier revision of this
PR added a bounded retry/backoff to `safe_copy`. It was dropped: the
full-parse fallback is the real safety net (it already makes the race
non-fatal), while a retry only salvages the *performance* of partial
parse in the rare `ESTALE` window — at the cost of adding heuristic
retry/backoff/sleep logic to a generic, widely-used utility that other
callers share. If the full-parse fallback ever proves too costly under
heavy NFS contention, a retry can be re-added later with constants tuned
from real traces.

## Related Issue(s)

Follow-up to #2815. Related to the partial-parse race in #971 / #972.

message:
Replace redirecting documentation URLs and raise lychee link-check timeout (#2905)

## Description

The docs `linkcheck` CI job (lychee) intermittently fails when a
documentation CDN is slow to respond: the stalled request is counted as
a timeout and fails the whole job even when no link is broken. This
surfaced on an unrelated PR, where the only failure was a single timeout
on `https://docs.astronomer.io/learn/scheduling-in-airflow` with 0
broken links:


https://github.com/astronomer/astronomer-cosmos/actions/runs/29727786982/job/88304791512?pr=2891

This PR makes two changes:

- **Replace 37 redirecting documentation URLs with their resolved
targets**, removing one network hop per link. Examples:
`cloud.google.com` → `docs.cloud.google.com`,
`github.com/.../raw/main/...` →
`raw.githubusercontent.com/.../main/...`, `docs.astronomer.io/learn/...`
→ `www.astronomer.io/docs/learn/...`, plus `docs.getdbt.com`,
`docs.microsoft.com` → `learn.microsoft.com`, and `docs.docker.com` path
moves.
- **Raise the lychee `timeout` from 30s to 60s** so occasionally-slow
hosts have enough headroom to respond before a request is counted as a
job-failing timeout.

`docs/**/*.rst` check reports 0 errors, with redirects followed dropping

subject: Fix CI dependency cache (cache uv's cache dir; stop keying on the version) (#2931)
message:
Fix CI dependency cache (cache uv's cache dir; stop keying on the version) (#2931)

## Summary

The `actions/cache` steps across `test.yml` + `test-unprivileged.yml`
intend to cache the Python deps, but three things make them ineffective:

1. **`path: .local/share/hatch/` is workspace-relative** → resolves to
`$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.local/share/hatch`, not hatch's data dir
(`$HOME/.local/share/hatch`) on the runner. So nothing is cached there.
2. **Installs run via `uv`** (`uv pip install -r …`), whose cache is
`~/.cache/uv` — which was never cached (only `~/.cache/pip`, which uv
doesn't use). So every job re-downloads/rebuilds ~479 packages.
3. **Keys end in `hashFiles('cosmos/__init__.py')`** — the version file
— so every release/version bump cold-busts *all* caches.

## Fix (~10 cache steps, both workflows)
- Cache **`~/.cache/uv`** instead of the dead workspace-relative hatch
path — `uv` hardlinks from its content-addressed cache instead of
re-downloading.
- Drop `hashFiles('cosmos/__init__.py')` from the keys so version bumps
don't invalidate them (`hashFiles('pyproject.toml')` still busts on real
dependency/config changes).

**Deliberately not caching the full hatch venv:** at this matrix scale
(~26 integration + unit/perf/etc. keys × ~1–2 GB each) it would exceed
the 10 GB repo cache budget and thrash (net-negative). Caching uv's
deduplicated cache gives most of the win at a fraction of the size.

## Validation
GitHub-Actions cache behaviour can't be reproduced locally, so this is
**draft** until CI confirms it. To measure: compare the **"Install
packages and dependencies"** step duration on a warm-cache run before vs
after (expect it to drop from a full ~479-pkg install to a fast uv-cache
restore). First run after merge is cold (cache written at job end); the
win shows on subsequent pushes.

subject: Add DAG-bundle hint when a dbt project path is missing (#2921)
message:
Add DAG-bundle hint when a dbt project path is missing (#2921)

On Airflow 3, DAGs can run from a **versioned DAG bundle** (e.g. an
Astronomer deployment or a git-based bundle) whose filesystem location
differs between DAG parsing and task execution. A hardcoded **absolute**
`dbt_project_path` that resolves at parse time can therefore be missing
on the worker, surfacing as a bare `FileNotFoundError` that is hard for
support/CRE to triage from logs alone.

This PR enriches the two places the missing-project error is raised so
the log is self-explanatory:

- `ProjectConfig.validate_project()` and `create_symlinks()` now append
a hint — **on Airflow 3, for an absolute path** — telling the user to
set `dbt_project_path` relative to their DAG file, e.g.
`(Path(__file__).parent / "dbt/my_dbt_project").absolute().as_posix()`,
linking the Astro getting-started docs.
- `create_symlinks()` now raises `CosmosValueError` instead of a bare
`FileNotFoundError` when the project directory does not exist.

## Why absolute-path detection alone isn't enough

The officially recommended pattern (`(Path(__file__).parent /
…).absolute()`) is itself an absolute path, so a proactive "you used an
absolute path" warning would false-positive on the correct usage. The
reliable signal is the actual "path not found" failure, which is what
this PR enriches.

## Detecting Astronomer

When running on Astronomer, the hint is **definitive** ("you are running
on Astronomer … the versioned bundle relocates the project"); otherwise
it stays **conditional** so it remains accurate for non-versioned
bundles (e.g. the default `dags-folder` bundle, which does not
relocate).

Astronomer is detected via `settings.in_astro`, which keys on the
**presence** of the `ASTRONOMER_ENVIRONMENT` variable rather than its
value. The Astronomer Runtime sets it on every Astro image (`cloud` on
hosted deployments, `local` for local dev) and it is present on workers,
where the runtime failure occurs. It is an *undocumented* platform
variable, so keying on presence — not on `"cloud"` — keeps the check
working if Astronomer introduces new values, while a generic Airflow-3
fallback still fires when it is absent.

To avoid a circular import (`cosmos.config` is imported very early via
the plugin/listeners, and a module-level import of `cosmos.dbt.project`
pulls in a partially-initialised `cosmos.settings`),
`validate_project()` imports the hint helper lazily.

## Testing

- New unit tests for the hint gating (Airflow 3 vs 2, absolute vs
relative vs `None`) and the incisive-vs-conditional wording, plus
`create_symlinks` raising `CosmosValueError` with the hint.
- Updated `test_validate_project_missing_fails` to be version-aware.
- Verified: AF2 (`py3.11-2.10-1.9`) full unit suite green; AF3
(`py3.11-3.0-1.9`) touched files green; mypy, pre-commit, and docs build
all pass.
- Live-verified in cosmos-demo on Astro Runtime 3.2
(`ASTRONOMER_ENVIRONMENT=local`, so `in_astro=True`): a DAG with a
hardcoded absolute `dbt_project_path` fails to parse with the incisive
message, while a DAG deriving the path from `Path(__file__)` parses
cleanly.

## Related issues

Closes astronomer/oss-integrations-private#418

Closes BOSS-382 —
https://linear.app/astronomer/issue/BOSS-382/improved-cosmos-logging-for-common-failure-modes

subject: Reduce `create_test_task_metadata` complexity (#2933)
message:
Reduce `create_test_task_metadata` complexity (#2933)

## Summary

Extract the WATCHER-aware test operator-class resolution out of
`create_test_task_metadata` into a small
`_calculate_test_operator_class` helper, to reduce the function's
cyclomatic complexity.

## Why

`create_test_task_metadata` currently sits at complexity **exactly 10**,
which is the ruff `C901` ceiling (`mccabe.max-complexity = 10`). It
passes on `main` today, but it has **zero headroom**: any added branch
tips it to 11 and fails CI. This already bit #2920, whose one-line
`on_warning_callback` fix trips `C901` (11 > 10) purely because the
function was at the limit.

Rather than `# noqa` the symptom, this gives the function room to
breathe.

## Change

Pure, behavior-preserving extraction:
- New module-level `_WATCHER_TO_FALLBACK_EXECUTION_MODE ` map +
`_calculate_test_operator_class(execution_mode, render_config)` helper
holding the exact same AFTER_ALL / WATCHER* logic (the `in
_WATCHER_TO_FALLBACK_EXECUTION_MODE ` membership check is the same set
as the original tuple).
- `create_test_task_metadata` now calls the helper.

Result: `create_test_task_metadata` drops from 10 to ~7; ruff `C901`,
`ruff check`, and `ruff format --check` all pass. No behavior change, so
the existing `create_test_task_metadata` tests cover it.

subject: Fix watcher multi-parent test aggregation: credit all parent models (#2901)
message:
Fix watcher multi-parent test aggregation: credit all parent models (#2901)

## Description

Under `ExecutionMode.WATCHER` + `TestBehavior.AFTER_EACH`, a dbt test
with more than
one parent model (e.g. a `relationships` test) is listed under every
parent in
`tests_per_model` but its result was credited to only the first parent
in
`accumulate_test_result` (early `return`). The other parent's
expected-test set never
completed, so its `<model>_tests_status` XCom was never pushed and its
test sensor
deferred until the producer terminated (then resolved unverified on
producer success,
or `PRODUCER_FAILED` on producer failure).

### Fix
`accumulate_test_result` had an early `return` that stopped at the first
parent. Drop it so
the result is recorded under every parent (return type `str | None` ->
`list[str]`), and have
`push_test_result_or_aggregate` aggregate/push for each parent returned.
Single-parent tests
are unchanged (the loop matches exactly one model); locking and keying
are untouched.

Tests: added regression coverage in
`tests/operators/_watcher/test_aggregation.py` (pass/fail
for a shared test, plus a no-shared-test control) and
`tests/dbt/test_graph.py`.

## Related Issue(s)

closes #2900 

## Breaking Change?

No.
